overview: Deere's fiscal Q3 net sales and revenues rose 5% to $12.608B, with a 14.4% equipment operations margin and net income of $1.379B, or $5.10 per diluted share, helped by $110M of incremental IEPA tariff refunds. Dan Pooley, Manager of Investor Communications, presented a raised fiscal 2026 net income guide of $4.75B-$5B, and Brent Norwood, CFO, reiterated that 2026 is the bottom of the ag cycle with a measured 2027 recovery.
keyTakeaways: Brent Norwood, CFO, said net tariffs become a headwind in fiscal 2027: about $750M net this year ($1.1B direct less $382M refunds) versus a run rate of about $1B next year.

Deanna Kovar, President of Worldwide Agriculture & Turf, said model year 2027 planter and sprayer early orders are up mid-single digits, with See & Spray adoption nearly doubling to about one-third of North American sprayers on order.

Chris Seibert, Director of Investor Relations, said Construction & Forestry holds four to five months of orders, more than the two to three Deere typically wants, with PPA and C&F each underproducing retail by a couple of points.
Kovar said South America demand is softer, with the industry cut to down 15%-20%, while used model-year 2023 and 2024 high horsepower tractors are down nearly 40% from a year ago.
financialHighlights: Equipment net sales up 6% to $10.999B; net income $1.379B, EPS $5.10; equipment operations margin 14.4%.
Production & Precision Ag sales down 6% to $3.998B at a 13.2% margin; Small Ag & Turf sales up 12% to $3.383B at an 18.4% margin.
Construction & Forestry sales up 18% to $3.618B at a 12.1% margin, including 8 points of price lapping about 5% negative price a year ago.
Financial Services net income $219M; IEPA refunds $110M in Q3 and $382M year to date.

keyMetrics.metric: MY2027 planter and sprayer early orders

guidance: Dan Pooley, Manager of Investor Communications, raised fiscal 2026 net income to $4.75B-$5B from $4.5B-$5B, equipment operations cash flow to $5B-$5.5B from $4.5B-$5.5B and Financial Services to $870M from $860M.
Pooley guided PPA sales down about 10% (from down 5%-10%) at an 11%-12% margin, SAT up about 15% at a 14.5%-15.5% margin (from 13.5%-15%), and C&F up about 20% at a 10.5%-11.5% margin.
Pooley cut South America industry sales to down 15%-20% and Europe to about flat, and raised U.S. and Canada construction to up 5%-10%.
Brent Norwood, CFO, expects Q4 PPA and C&F sales similar to Q3 with no refund benefit and seasonally higher R&D and SA&G, and a fiscal 2027 net tariff run rate around $1B.
risksMentioned: Net tariff expense steps up to about $1B in fiscal 2027 from about $750M, per Norwood.
South America and Europe ag softness, with Brazil's industry down 15%-20% and European arable farmers more challenged, per Kovar and Seibert.
Input cost and commodity volatility, including fertilizer uncertainty and Black Sea shipment disruptions, per Seibert and Kovar.
Inflation remains dynamic given oil prices and suppliers passing on tariffs, per Seibert.

qa.question: Is the roughly $800M net tariff impact this year a headwind, tailwind or neutral going into 2027?
qa.answer: A headwind: about $1.1B of direct tariffs less $382M of refunds gives net exposure of approximately $750M this year, while the 2027 run rate is expected right around $1B.

qa.question: Did something slip from Q4 into Q3, and was tractor inventory built in Q3 ahead of the industry?
qa.answer: Not to read too much into Q3; some demand was pulled ahead to manage Q4 risk and nothing on inventory is concerning. Norwood said Q4 PPA and C&F sales should be similar to Q3 without the refund benefit and with seasonally high R&D and SA&G, so margins come in a little.
qa.read: Answered directly; disputed the inventory premise.

qa.question: Is the tariff estimate cut to $1.1B from relief or refunds, and how is the excavator launch trending?
qa.answer: Mainly Section 232 changes cutting the rate on imported goods from roughly 25% to 15% effective June 1, so only five of 12 months benefit this year with a further 2027 tailwind. Norwood: three Deere-designed excavator models are in market, with more over three to four years.

qa.question: Why does C&F guidance imply only about 50 bps of Q4 price after +8% in Q3, and how large should dealer rental fleets get?
qa.answer: The C&F price guide went 2.5% to 3% to 2.5% and back to 3%; Q3's 8% partly reflected about 5% negative price in Q3 2025. Norwood said 30%-35% of earthmoving transactions start as a rental and dealers want to expand fleets, with no target size.
qa.read: Answered partially; declined to size rental fleets.

unanswered.question: How should the 2027 mix impact be thought about versus the 2- to 3-point benefit in stronger years?
unanswered.how: Chris Seibert, Director of Investor Relations, said it is too early to tell, citing input volatility and E.U. and Brazil softness.

unanswered.question: Does the backlog imply margins up, down or neutral next year?
unanswered.how: Seibert spoke to covering inflation with measured pricing and gave no margin direction.

unanswered.question: Can Deere give a directional 2027 forecast for Europe ahead of the 2028 CAP change?
unanswered.how: Seibert: "too early to tell"; the order book runs only four to five months out.
